purpose: Structured evidence ledger for the orthogonal art-gallery literature review.

sources.citation: M. Abrahamsen, A. Adamaszek, and T. Miltzow. The art gallery problem is exists-R-complete. Journal of the ACM 69(1), Article 4, 2022.
sources.relevant_result: The standard art-gallery decision problem is exists-R-complete, even for simple polygons with integer-coordinate vertices.
sources.translation_note: Use as modern complexity context only. It does not contradict extremal upper bounds for restricted orthogonal or lattice classes.
verification: Primary JACM article checked via Utrecht repository record.
Theorem 1 on article page 4:2 states the exists-R-completeness result; Theorem 13 on page 4:12 gives membership in exists-R.

sources.citation: N. M. Benbernou, E. D. Demaine, M. L. Demaine, A. Kurdia, J. O'Rourke, G. T. Toussaint, J. Urrutia, and G. Viglietta. Edge-guarding orthogonal polyhedra. CCCG 2011.
sources.relevant_result: Theorem 5 proves that every orthogonal polyhedron with e total edges and r reflex edges is guardable by floor((e+r)/12) open edge guards; Corollaries 6 and 7 imply open-edge-guard bounds of (11/72)e - g/6 - 1 and (7/12)r - g + 1.
sources.translation_note: This is a 3D edge-guard result, not a point-guard or perimeter result. The (7/12)r expression is parameterized by the number of reflex edges; it is not a theorem using only reflex-edge guards.
verification: Primary CCCG 2011 PDF checked from the O'Rourke author page.

Theorem 5, PDF pp. 5-6, proves the floor((e+r)/12) open-edge-guard bound; Corollaries 6 and 7, PDF p. 6, give the (11/72)e - g/6 - 1 and (7/12)r - g + 1 consequences. Theorem 2, PDF pp. 3-4, supplies the e/r/genus relation, and Theorem 4, PDF pp. 4-5, relates open and closed edge guards.

sources.citation: T. C. Biedl, M. T. Irfan, J. Iwerks, J. Kim, and J. S. B. Mitchell. The art gallery theorem for polyominoes. Discrete & Computational Geometry 48, 711--720, 2012.
sources.relevant_result: Every m-cell polyomino, possibly with holes, can be guarded by floor((m+1)/3) point guards; the bound is sometimes necessary.
sources.translation_note: This is an area/cell-count theorem. It does not imply a perimeter-over-six theorem because area and perimeter are incomparable for the needed extremal question.
verification: University publication page states the m-cell bound and that holes are allowed.

sources.citation: T. Biedl, T. M. Chan, S. Lee, S. Mehrabi, F. Montecchiani, H. Vosoughpour, and Z. Yu. Guarding orthogonal art galleries with sliding k-transmitters: hardness and approximation. Algorithmica 81(1), 69--97, 2019.
sources.relevant_result: Studies hardness and approximation for guarding orthogonal art galleries with sliding k-transmitters.
sources.translation_note: Related visibility model only. Do not cite it as evidence for standard point-guard perimeter bounds.
verification: DOI recorded; used for algorithmic/restricted-visibility context.

sources.citation: I. Bjorling-Sachs. Edge guards in rectilinear polygons. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 11(2), 111--123, 1998.
sources.relevant_result: Provides a tight edge-guard theorem for rectilinear polygons.
sources.translation_note: Useful 2D edge-guard reference point. It should not be confused with 2D point guards or 3D edge guards.
verification: DOI recorded; exact theorem should be checked against primary PDF if further expanded.

sources.citation: J. Cano, C. D. Toth, J. Urrutia, and G. Viglietta. Edge guards for polyhedra in three-space. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 104, 101859, 2022.
sources.relevant_result: Every polyhedron with m edges can be guarded by at most (5/6)m edge guards; the paper emphasizes the remaining gap to lower bounds.
sources.translation_note: General 3D edge-guard result. For this review it frames the broader 3D gap around the sharper orthogonal-polyhedron conjectures.
verification: Search result confirmed the general m-edge context and open gap.

sources.citation: V. Chvatal. A combinatorial theorem in plane geometry. Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 18(1), 39--41, 1975.
sources.venue: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B
sources.relevant_result: Every simple n-vertex polygon can be guarded by floor(n/3) point guards, and this is tight.
sources.translation_note: Foundational non-orthogonal bound. It is weaker than the orthogonal n/4 theorem and unrelated to lattice perimeter.

sources.citation: J. M. Diaz-Banez, P. Horn, M. A. Lopez, N. Marin, A. Ramirez-Vigueras, O. Sole-Pi, A. Stevens, and J. Urrutia. Ortho-unit polygons can be guarded with at most floor((n-4)/8) guards. Graphs and Combinatorics 41, 15, 2025.
sources.relevant_result: Every ortho-unit polygon with n >= 12 vertices can be guarded by floor((n-4)/8) guards, tightly. The paper also frames an integral-perimeter N/6 direction.
sources.translation_note: The ortho-unit theorem is stronger than perimeter/6 in that narrow unit-edge model. The hole-free integral N/6 reading is covered by Massberg after subdivision; only holes or broader lattice-domain readings remain open.

sources.citation: S. Durocher, O. Filtser, R. Fraser, A. D. Mehrabi, and S. Mehrabi. Guarding orthogonal art galleries with sliding cameras. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 65, 12--26, 2017.
sources.relevant_result: Develops results for sliding-camera guarding in orthogonal art galleries.
sources.translation_note: Related model only. It supplies algorithmic context, not a standard point-guard perimeter theorem.
verification: DOI recorded; exact theorem breakdown should be primary-checked for deeper algorithmic section.

sources.citation: O. Filtser, E. Krohn, B. J. Nilsson, C. Rieck, and C. Schmidt. Guarding polyominoes under k-hop visibility. Algorithmica 87, 572--593, 2025.
sources.relevant_result: Studies guarding polyominoes under k-hop visibility, including algorithmic and approximation questions.
sources.translation_note: Discrete visibility variant. Useful for adjacent open problems but not evidence for straight-line point-guard perimeter-over-six.
verification: Springer page summary checked during web search.

sources.citation: S. Fisk. A short proof of Chvatal's watchman theorem. Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 24(3), 374, 1978.
sources.venue: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B
sources.relevant_result: Gives the short triangulation and three-coloring proof of Chvatal's floor(n/3) theorem.
sources.translation_note: Proof-template reference for coloring arguments. It is not an orthogonal, hole, or perimeter result.

sources.citation: S. K. Ghosh. Approximation algorithms for art gallery problems in polygons. Journal of Discrete Algorithms 8(1), 2010.
sources.relevant_result: Surveys/develops approximation-algorithm context for art-gallery problems.
sources.translation_note: Use for algorithmic landscape and approximation context. It should not be used to state extremal perimeter bounds.

sources.citation: E. Gyori. A short proof of the rectilinear art gallery theorem. SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods 7(3), 452--454, 1986.
sources.venue: SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods
sources.relevant_result: Provides a short proof of the floor(n/4) rectilinear art-gallery theorem.
sources.translation_note: Vertex-count theorem for simple orthogonal polygons. It does not address holes or lattice perimeter.

sources.citation: F. Hoffmann and K. Kriegel. A graph-coloring result and its consequences for polygon-guarding problems. SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 9(2), 210--224, 1996.
sources.relevant_result: Uses graph coloring to obtain guarding bounds for polygon-guarding problems, including orthogonal polygons with holes.
sources.translation_note: Relevant to hole/vertex-guard context. It is not a point-guard perimeter theorem.
verification: Urrutia open-problem page cites Hoffmann-style floor(2n/7) conjecture.

sources.citation: J. Kahn, M. Klawe, and D. Kleitman. Traditional galleries require fewer watchmen. SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods 4(2), 194--206, 1983.
sources.venue: SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods
sources.relevant_result: Every simple orthogonal n-vertex polygon is guardable by floor(n/4) point guards, and the bound is tight.
sources.translation_note: Core 2D orthogonal theorem. It is a vertex-count result for simple polygons; holes and perimeter are separate.

sources.citation: M. J. Katz and G. S. Roisman. On guarding the vertices of rectilinear domains. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 39(3), 219--228, 2008.
sources.relevant_result: Studies guarding vertices of rectilinear domains and associated hardness.
sources.translation_note: Algorithmic context for rectilinear domains. Do not translate to extremal perimeter sufficiency.

sources.citation: D. T. Lee and A. K. Lin. Computational complexity of art gallery problems. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 32(2), 276--282, 1986.
sources.relevant_result: Classical NP-hardness framework for art-gallery optimization problems.
sources.translation_note: Use to separate minimum-guard computation from worst-case existence theorems.
verification: DOI recorded; exact title and venue checked.

sources.citation: J. Massberg. Perfect graphs and guarding rectilinear art galleries. Discrete & Computational Geometry 51, 569--577, 2014.
sources.relevant_result: A hole-free polyomino with perimeter ell >= 6 can be guarded by at most floor(ell/6) point guards; the bound is tight.
sources.translation_note: This is the central perimeter-over-six theorem. It covers hole-free integral orthogonal polygons after unit-grid subdivision. It does not prove the hole case.
verification: Search result summary confirmed the perimeter ell >= 6 statement.

sources.citation: J. Massberg. Perfect graphs and related topics: habilitation thesis, including Conjecture 6.10. Ulm University, 2013.
sources.relevant_result: States a maximal-rectangle packing conjecture whose truth would extend the perimeter-over-six method to hole cases.
sources.translation_note: This is the key source for conditional/open status. It is not itself a proof of perimeter-over-six with holes.
verification: Web search snippet confirmed Conjecture 6.10 and a hole example where maximal-rectangle graph perfection fails.

sources.citation: T. S. Michael and V. Pinciu. How to guard orthogonal polygons: diagonal graphs and vertex covers. Discrete & Computational Geometry 55(2), 410--422, 2016.
sources.relevant_result: Introduces same-sign diagonal graphs and vertex-cover methods, including h-independent upper bounds such as floor((17n-8)/52) for orthogonal polygons with holes.
sources.translation_note: Important improvement for holes in vertex-count frameworks. It does not settle perimeter-over-six point guards.
verification: Exact-title searches confirmed the diagonal graph and vertex cover framework.

sources.citation: R. Motwani, A. Raghunathan, and H. Saran. Covering orthogonal polygons with star polygons: The perfect graph approach. Journal of Computer and System Sciences 40(1), 19--48, 1990.
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
sources.relevant_result: Develops perfect-graph methods for covering orthogonal polygons with star polygons.
sources.translation_note: Proof-technology source for later rectangle/perfect-graph approaches; not directly a perimeter theorem.

sources.citation: J. O'Rourke. Art Gallery Theorems and Algorithms. Oxford University Press, 1987.
sources.relevant_result: Standard book reference for art-gallery theorems, algorithms, visibility, rectilinear galleries, holes, and early 3D context.
sources.translation_note: Use as background and for classical bounds. When citing a theorem, prefer the original source as well.

sources.citation: M. S. Paterson and F. F. Yao. Optimal binary space partitions for orthogonal objects. Journal of Algorithms 13(1), 99--113, 1992.
sources.relevant_result: Binary-space partition result used in the 3D guarding literature to obtain tight Theta(n^(3/2)) point-guard behavior for orthogonal polyhedra.
sources.translation_note: This blocks a direct linear point-guard analogue in 3D and motivates edge/reflex-edge models.
verification: DOI recorded; review currently relies on Viglietta for the guard-theorem translation.

sources.citation: V. Pinciu. Guarding polyominoes, polycubes and polyhypercubes. Electronic Notes in Discrete Mathematics 49, 159--166, 2015.
sources.relevant_result: Studies guarding in discrete polyform families including polyominoes, polycubes, and polyhypercubes.
sources.translation_note: Useful for discrete 3D analogues. It is not the continuous orthogonal-polyhedron point-guard model.
verification: DOI recorded; primary details should be checked before stating exact bounds.

sources.citation: D. Schuchardt and H.-D. Hecker. Two NP-hard art-gallery problems for orthogonal polygons. Mathematical Logic Quarterly 41(2), 261--267, 1995.
sources.relevant_result: Proves NP-hardness for two art-gallery problems restricted to orthogonal polygons.
sources.translation_note: Optimization-hardness evidence only. It does not negate existential upper bounds.

sources.citation: T. C. Shermer. Recent results in art galleries. Proceedings of the IEEE 80(9), 1384--1399, 1992.
sources.relevant_result: Surveys art-gallery results and open problems, including hole-related conjectural directions.
sources.translation_note: Use for historical survey context. For current open status, pair with Urrutia's open-problem page and later papers.

sources.citation: J. Urrutia. Art gallery and illumination problems. Handbook of Computational Geometry, 973--1027, Elsevier, 2000.
sources.relevant_result: Comprehensive survey chapter for art-gallery and illumination problems.
sources.translation_note: Use for background and variant taxonomy; cite original sources for exact theorem statements.

sources.citation: J. Urrutia. Illumination of polygons: open problems.
sources.relevant_result: Records Shermer's floor((n+h)/4) vertex-guard conjecture and Hoffmann's floor(2n/7) vertex-guard conjecture for orthogonal polygons with holes.
sources.translation_note: This is the direct open-problem source for 2D orthogonal holes with vertex guards. It is adjacent to but distinct from point-guard perimeter-over-six.
verification: Open-problem page checked in web search.

sources.citation: G. Viglietta. Guarding and searching polyhedra. Ph.D. thesis; arXiv:1211.2483, 2012.
sources.relevant_result: Central 3D guarding/searching reference; presents the point-guard obstruction and Urrutia-type edge/reflex-edge conjectures.
sources.translation_note: Use as the bridge from Paterson-Yao BSP results to guarding orthogonal polyhedra, and as a source for 3D open-problem formulations.

sources.citation: G. Viglietta. Face-guarding polyhedra. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 47(8), 833--846, 2014.
sources.relevant_result: Studies face-guarding for several classes of polyhedra, including orthogonal subclasses.
sources.translation_note: Maps the 3D model space but should not be merged with edge-guard or point-guard statements.

sources.citation: G. Viglietta. Optimally guarding 2-reflex orthogonal polyhedra by reflex edge guards. Computational Geometry: Theory and Applications 86, 101589, 2020.
sources.relevant_result: For 2-reflex orthogonal polyhedra, proves tight-style reflex-edge guard bounds and an O(n log n) guard-placement algorithm.
sources.translation_note: Strong partial result for a restricted 3D class. It does not settle general 3-reflex orthogonal polyhedra.
verification: Search result confirmed the 2-reflex restriction and algorithmic statement.

sources.citation: C. Worman and J. M. Keil. Polygon decomposition and the orthogonal art gallery problem. International Journal of Computational Geometry & Applications 17(2), 105--138, 2007.
sources.venue: International Journal of Computational Geometry & Applications
sources.relevant_result: Develops polygon decomposition and visibility-graph machinery for orthogonal art-gallery problems.
sources.translation_note: Methodological source for decomposition approaches; exact downstream theorem use should be primary-checked before adding new claims.

sources.citation: P. Zylinski. Orthogonal art galleries with holes: A coloring proof of Aggarwal's theorem. Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 13(1), R20, 2006.
sources.relevant_result: Gives a coloring proof of Aggarwal's theorem: floor((n+h)/4) vertex guards suffice for orthogonal polygons with h <= 2 holes and for cactus-dual quadrilateralizations.
sources.translation_note: Partial positive result for Shermer-type vertex-guard conjectures. It does not settle arbitrary holes or point-guard perimeter bounds.
verification: DOI and public journal page recorded.
Web search result confirmed the h <= 2 / cactus-dual scope.
